title: Monotonic Stack: Find the Next Greater Element
oneLiner: For every element, find the next one to its right that's bigger -- a stack that only ever holds a decreasing sequence answers this for the WHOLE array in one pass.
keyTakeaway: A monotonic stack keeps its elements in one-way order (each no larger, or each no smaller, than the one below it) at all times by popping anything that violates that order BEFORE pushing the new element -- each element gets pushed once and popped at most once, so the whole array is processed in O(n) total despite looking like a nested loop problem.
explanation:
"Find the next greater element" for every position in an array -- naively, that's a nested loop: for each index, scan RIGHT until something bigger shows up, O(n^2) worst case. A MONOTONIC STACK solves it in one O(n) pass: walk the array left to right, and before pushing the current element's index onto the stack, pop off every index whose value is SMALLER than the current element -- each one just found its "next greater element": the current one.

The stack stays monotonically NON-INCREASING (bottom to top; equal values stay) at all times, by construction -- anything that would break that order gets popped and resolved immediately, before the new element goes on. Whatever's left on the stack at the very end never found a next-greater element (nothing to their right was ever bigger), so those get whatever "no answer" value the problem wants (often -1).

The O(n) part is the subtle bit: it LOOKS like a nested loop (an inner while-pop loop inside the outer for-loop), but every single element gets pushed exactly once and popped AT MOST once across the entire run -- so the total number of pop operations across the whole algorithm is bounded by n, not n per outer iteration. Watch the stack below: notice it only ever holds a decreasing run of not-yet-resolved elements.

starterCode.python:
def next_greater_elements(nums):
    # TODO: result = list of -1s, same length as nums. Walk a stack of
    # INDICES left to right. Before pushing index i, pop every index j on
    # the stack whose nums[j] < nums[i] -- each one's answer is nums[i].
    # Whatever's left on the stack at the end keeps -1.
    return []

nums[3]=4 > nums[2]=2 -- pop index 2, its next greater is 4.
nums[3]=4 > nums[0]=2 -- pop index 0, its next greater is 4.
Push index 3 (val 4) -- stack stays non-increasing bottom to top.
Push index 4 (val 3) -- stack stays non-increasing bottom to top.
Done -- result: [4, 2, 4, -1, -1]. Anything left on the stack never found a next greater element.

recognitionSignals: The problem asks for the "next greater/smaller element" for every position in an array.
You're about to write a nested loop scanning right (or left) from every index -- an O(n^2) shape a monotonic stack collapses to O(n).
gotchas: Push INDICES onto the stack, not values -- you need the index later to write into the result array at the right position.
Using <= instead of < (or vice versa) in the pop condition silently changes whether equal elements count as "greater" -- match whatever the problem actually asks for.
confusableWith: Two Pointers / Sliding Window (this track) also make one pass over an array, but with pointers moving independently or a window boundary sliding -- a monotonic stack's defining feature is the stack itself staying ordered at all times.

complexity.note: Looks like a nested loop but isn't: each index is pushed once and popped at most once, so total work is about 2n; the stack can hold up to n indices.
